headline: KEPCO confirmed exposure for 650,487 billing users, Guadeloupe University Hospital postponed non-urgent care after a cyberattack, and Samsung Securities confirmed exposure affecting 8,241 people. In an update to its earlier breach, Kurly identified 199 current or former employees and two more customers whose information was exposed.

incidents.what: KEPCO confirmed exposure for 650,487 billing users and notified all 869,761 procurement users while it investigates the scope of the breach in that system.
The hospital director said encrypted databases and disrupted phones and clinical systems forced three sites to postpone non-urgent care.
The brokerage confirmed that an intrusion into its customer feedback system exposed personal information, including some account and driver’s license numbers.
The Block estimated about $2 million in attacker proceeds and separately valued later withdrawals from Fusionist’s bridge reserves at about $3.7 million.
Police took the network offline after detecting a potential database intrusion; phones, radio and calls for service continued normally.
incidents.scale: Network offline; no evidence of personal data access

incidents.org: Sri Lanka Department of Motor Traffic
incidents.what: The department said its public website was attacked but its separate appointment service stayed operational.
incidents.scale: Appointments unaffected; data exposure not disclosed

incidents.what: Hyflock claimed it took data from Samsung Group; no independent confirmation was found.
One X account alleged new unauthorized NES minting and estimated about $440,000 in sale proceeds; no independent or project confirmation was found.
Chainflip offered a 10% bounty for returning funds by November 23 at 18:38 UTC; the combined theft is estimated at about $12 million, with no return reported.
incidents.scale: About $12M estimated across Ethereum and Bitcoin

incidents.what: A Cleverbridge notice reviewed by BleepingComputer said the stolen payment data included card numbers, expiry dates and security codes.
A review of the November breach identified another 199 current or former employees and two customers whose information was exposed.
Voi Network published its account of the losses and said withdrawals stopped after Aramid secured the affected bridge accounts.
